newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka troops in fresh push against rebels.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka troops in fresh push against rebels.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops have resumed an offensive against Tamil separatists, meeting negligible resistance as they pushed deeper into rebel-held territory, military officials said on Tuesday.
"Troops moved about eight km (five miles) west without meeting resistance," a military spokesman said in Colombo.
The Defence Ministry has declined to reveal the aim of the latest offensive, which was initially launched on February 4 from Vavuniya, a government stronghold 220 km (138 miles) northeast of Colombo.

The drive resumed on Monday, military officials said, after troops paused for about 10 days to fortify its gains following a 22-km (14-mile) push into rebel territory during the first three days of the offensive, code-named "Edi Bala" (brave force).

"Within 12 hours (after resumption), troops backed by air cover and heavy artillery moved swiftly to cover a distance of 10 kilometres with hardly any resistance from the enemy," the government-owned Daily News said on Tuesday.
Rebel resistance so far has been light and the army has had no casualties in the offensive, the military spokesman said.
The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in this predominantly Sinhalese Indian Ocean island, were not immediately available for comment.
Troops also killed two rebels early on Tuesday in an ambush near Valachchenai, 240 km (150 miles) east of Colombo, military officials in the area said.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE says the toll is much higher.
